Keying sets alpha 0 but leaves the key colour in RGB, and the GPU does not consult alpha when it filters — SpriteMaterial bilinear filtering and mipmaps average RGB across neighbours, so pure ff00ff under the transparency bleeds into every edge texel surviving alphaTest, worst on thin features where downscaling averages one real texel against several key texels. Measured: 100% of transparent pixels held key-magenta RGB, including 3982/1540/1755 directly touching visible art. The already-shipped prop-baron-banner.png carries the IDENTICAL property (4128), so the fault was extract-alpha.mjs and the fix is class-level: bleedEdges() propagates visible colour outward under the transparency to exhaustion, never touching alpha — transparent/opaque/partial counts and subject bboxes are identical before and after, so the cut-out shape is bit-for-bit the same. After: key-magenta under transparency 100% -> 0%. THE PROBE WAS NOT WRONG, ITS QUESTION WAS: it asked whether magenta survived among the VISIBLE pixels and truthfully answered 0. LOOKING is what caught it (F-1446-1). tasks.authorNotes: PREMISE AND CURE BOTH MEASURED BY THE AUTHORING FIRE, NOT PROPOSED FROM THEORY. Three arms, same machine, same session: pre-merge main (13 files, spawnSync) 72 tests 0/6 red; merged (15 files, spawnSync) 74 tests 4/11 red; merged + prototype cure 74 tests 0/8 red. Every failure is whole suite collects without loading Vite-only modules, twice directly and twice nested inside the new meta-guard. Mechanism verified at the captured bytes: the failing assertion is assert.match(result.stdout, /Total: [1-9]\d* tests/) while result.status is 0 and the listing is well-formed — the capture is simply truncated before the trailing Total: line. Full solo capture 296,028 bytes; failing captures ~153,474 chars (ending mid-line at assay-ledger-page.spec.ts:80:1) and ~156,216 chars. TWO DIFFERENT TRUNCATION POINTS = A RACE, NOT A BOUNDARY, and NOT maxBuffer (296 KB is under the 1 MB default, and overflow would set ENOBUFS + null status). Four concurrent execFile listings return the full 296,028 bytes every time, so the defect follows the SYNCHRONOUS capture. THE OLD GREEN WAS A FALSE GREEN — the meta-guard did not create the race, it exposed it, so do NOT cure this by lightening the battery, and the meta-guard is explicitly OUT of firewall as the detector rather than the fault. ANTI-SCOPE: neither /Total: [1-9]\d* tests/ regex may be touched — both are correct and were already refuted as a phantom defect in s1201 (F-1201-1); this would be the second run to cure a regex that was never broken. The observe-first gate is scope 1 and warns that a QUIET MACHINE CAN HIDE A LOAD-DEPENDENT RACE, so 8/8 green is not a STOP by itself — re-run under load, and proceed to scope 2 regardless because the truncation mechanism is verified independently of the flake rate.

tasks.drainNotes: s1210. ACCEPTED, AND IT IS BETTER THAN ITS OWN REPORT CLAIMED. The cure moves the control loop INSIDE the page — one page.evaluate dispatches keydown then samples __THREE_GAME_DIAGNOSTICS__ every 16ms in-browser, releasing on a speed-aware lead (speed/28 + 0.08) and resolving only once the hero has actually stopped — so accuracy no longer depends on round-trip latency, which is exactly the mechanism s1207 measured (166-491ms against an intended 25ms loop). The outer loop re-picks the dominant axis over up to 12 attempts and converges on hypot(dx,dz)<=0.12 instead of per-axis inequalities, curing the 'one pass per axis, never re-check x after z' defect; it also dismisses a levelup overlay that could eat the movement. GATES: tsc 0 · build green 1.38s · e2e/release-build.spec.ts under its REAL config 24/26. Runner's retained numbers: approach failures 5/8 (62.5%) -> 0/8, 72/72 movements converged, and a MUTATION CONTROL (12 attempts -> 3) restored 6/8 — a guard shown failing, not only passing. TEST-ONLY SLICE, no src/ touched. Base 4fdbc950 is an ancestor of main and `git diff 4fdbc950 main` on both paths is EMPTY, so both files applied clean with no 3-way. ⚠️ F-1210-5: the 2 residual failures at release-build.spec.ts:21 are NOT this slice's — they are GG-01b's, proved by a one-variable control this fire (cure + GG-01b = 2/2 FAIL on 'town-open-board not visible'; cure - GG-01b = 2/2 PASS in 57.9s). The runner's honest 'inventory remains red' note therefore under-credits its own cure. ⚠️ F-1210-6 (mine, disclosed): this slice landed as an UNLABELLED SWEEP inside 0b8db8f9 — `git checkout c162bd1a -- <paths>` stages what it writes, and a later plain `git commit` took the whole index, so a commit whose message names only GG-01b ledger work also carries this cure. Content correct and fully gated; the message is wrong, and this review is the correction. HARNESS LESSON WORTH THE LEDGER: e2e/release-build.spec.ts runs ONLY under playwright.release.config.ts (vite preview on 5190). Run under the default dev config it fails 10/10 including 'dist has no later manifest ids', a test no graft could affect — a red inherits its harness config.

IT IS A CLASS, NOT THE TRAIL GUIDE BUG: grep -rln pressUntil e2e/ returns release-build.spec.ts as the ORIGIN (9 call sites, :303 is literally moveHeroTo(page,-9,6.7), the exact target the trace measured), and suite-red-inventory.md:198 already carries e2e/release-build.spec.ts:297 | Error: Hero blocked while moving KeyW as an unexplained known-red — :297 is a call site and that string is the pressUntil throw verbatim, so curing the helper converts a documented mystery into an explained fix. tasks.title: F-1523-6 corrective: the F-1522-1 dispatch guard must refuse on non-zero line-level RESIDUE, not on the coarse blob-identity HOLDS word — lane-b holds 0 absent lines on every held path and the merged guard would refuse it
tasks.authorNotes: AUTHORED FROM THIS FIRE'S OWN MERGE, one hour after landing the thing it corrects. s1523 merged c81c15841 (the F-1522-1 pre-dispatch guard, refusing on a positive HOLDS). THE GUARD IS NOT WRONG — it does exactly what its master specified and all five fixture arms pass. The defect is that HOLDS is computed at a COARSER RESOLUTION than the question the guard asks it. READ FROM scripts/lane-usable.mjs, NOT INFERRED: held is built at BLOB IDENTITY (a path is HELD unless the lane blob equals main's, or the lane never moved it), while the line-level residue that every fire reads as '(N of M added lines absent from main)' is computed by residueForHeld/formatHeldResidue FOR DISPLAY ONLY and never feeds the verdict ladder. So a lane whose every added line is already on main, but whose files main moved FURTHER, reads HOLDS. MEASURED ON THE LIVE FLEET by replaying the merged guard's own sed extraction: lane-a rc=2 HOLDS (lb-01 spec 0 of 13 absent), lane-b rc=2 HOLDS (lb-01 spec 0 of 43 absent, BACKLOG 0 of 1 absent), lane-c USABLE, lane-d AHEAD-BUT-ABSORBED. lane-absorbed-lines.mjs answers in one command that BOTH of lane-b's held paths are ABSORBED. So the guard would refuse a lane holding nothing. URGENCY DESPITE INERTNESS: the guard activates only on runner restart, and F-1522-5 is on the owner's desk asking Robin for exactly that restart — if he does it today, two of four lanes are refused on their first dispatch with a message naming fully-absorbed paths, and the factory reads as broken by the commit meant to protect it. LIMIT STATED HONESTLY: this is NOT F-1027-1's permanent brick, because a fire can still archive+reset such a lane by hand; what it costs is that the ORDINARY POST-DRAIN STATE of a lane now needs manual intervention before reuse, which against a fast-moving main is the common case rather than the rare one. THE CURE MAY NOT TOUCH lane-usable.mjs — F-1212-4/F-1419-1 make its verdict words, RC map, CHURN set and RUN_SURFACE a standing prohibition, and widening AHEAD-BUT-ABSORBED would change the word's meaning under every other consumer including --cure's load-bearing refusal. The guard is the consumer that asked the wrong-resolution question, so the second question belongs in the guard. The master also specifies a DELIBERATE ASYMMETRY: the outer probe fails OPEN (a broken instrument must never stall the factory) while the inner residue probe fails CLOSED (an instrument that could not prove safety must not license a reset), and the runner is asked to confirm it understood this rather than merely implement it.

tasks.blockedReason: OWNER DESIGN FORK (F-1475-1) — the fairground era-socket cannot be PROVED without first deciding what SUPPORTED_CONTRACTS admission MEANS. THE MASTER WAS JOINTLY UNSATISFIABLE. lane-e3-fairground-socket.md line 98 told the runner to prove the socket "through the declared-mode path that bypasses the support gate" and to "reuse" the census spec mechanism — THAT MECHANISM DOES NOT EXIST: the string fairground appears exactly ONCE in e2e/er01-e3-census.spec.ts, at line 7 inside the gap record, and that file constructs no HeadlessContractSim for it. THE RUNNER WAS RIGHT TO STOP, AND THE MASTER PRE-AUTHORIZED THIS EXACT OUTCOME in the same sentence: "If it turns out no such path can drive your assertions without admitting the contract, STOP and report it as a finding — that is a genuine design fork about what admission means, and it belongs to the owner, not to this run." DO NOT RE-QUEUE THIS MASTER UNCHANGED. That would be an identical retry of a premise already proven false (§7.5 requires a CHANGED premise). The socket SCOPE (extracting a headlessly-constructible Fair Wheel core from src/entities/FerrisWheel.ts) remains sound and re-usable the moment the owner rules on the proof path.

One cheap evidence task closes the last gap and turns the whole thing into ONE art request. THE OPEN QUESTION, EXACTLY: the survey's table (report lines 105-106) records Rail Tough rows 2 AND 3 as UNCERTAIN with confidence NONE, because the BODY reads as a mirror pair (row 2 head/boots screen-left, row 3 screen-right = nw/ne) while the 2v3 silhouette IoU is DIRECT-dominant (+0.248), which means same heading. Two opposite answers from one run. THE MASTER'S CENTRAL IDEA IS THAT THE SILHOUETTE MAY BE THE THING THAT IS WRONG, and it supplies the mechanism rather than just the doubt: every instrument used on these sheets so far discards everything but the outline, and the Rail Tough is the ONE character of the three carrying a large one-hand prop. The survey itself validated the wrench as a STABLE BODY-SIDE prop (screen-left across front rows 0/1, screen-right across back rows 2/3). If rows 2/3 are a TRUE mirror pair, mirroring aligns the bodies but throws a large prop blob onto opposite sides, deflating the mirrored score and inflating the direct one — a big asymmetric prop can invert an IoU verdict on an otherwise near-symmetric walking figure. Both readings are therefore live and the master forbids assuming either. SCOPE 5 IS THE DECISIVE EXPERIMENT AND IS DESIGNED TO BE INFORMATIVE WHICHEVER WAY IT FALLS: mask the wrench out and re-run the SAME floor-calibrated IoU on 2v3; if removing the prop FLIPS the verdict to mirror-dominant, the silhouette was measuring the wrench and the visual read was right; if it stays direct-dominant, the rows really are duplicates. The before/after pair is the deliverable even if every row ends UNCERTAIN. METHOD BORROWED FROM THE PREDECESSOR'S BEST IDEA: use the SHIPPED CARDINAL sheet as ground truth to fix the wrench's body side from cardinal s/n independently of any diagonal ordering — the exact technique that converted the Steam Wrecker from unmeasurable to row-level — but with an added guard the survey did not need: RE-DERIVE the cardinal row order from assets/processed/char-railtough-sheet-walk4-a.frames.json rather than assuming row 0 is s, because citing an unverified row index is the error class this entire thread exists to correct. tasks.title: F-1319-3 root cause (s1320): terrainSeed() re-parses window.location.search into a NEW URLSearchParams and re-runs normalizeSeed on EVERY call (Terrain.ts:1619-1622); terrainHash calls it per hash, valueNoise calls terrainHash 4x, sample()/terrainFeatures call valueNoise ~9x — so ONE terrain sample costs ~36 URL parses. A --cpu-prof of one e1-night-shift episode attributes 67% of 19.85s to URL parsing (parseParams 41.4%, normalizeSeed 14.1%, URLSearchParams ctor 9.0%, get search 2.6%). Both of F-1319-3's hypotheses are REFUTED by measurement: construction/placeFree cost is indistinguishable between arms (nonTickMs 801-949ms vs 482-1178ms), and 7 working lanterns cost only +970ms while flipping the SAME seven to wrecked costs +16,730ms — wrecked instances alone fall through updateRepairs' cheap continue (BuildSystem.ts:2117) into terrainMaxForFootprint every tick, which is why they made it visible. Cure measured both ways, both bit-for-bit determinism-preserving (eventLogHash fnv1a32:c086ef19 unchanged): search-keyed cache 19,048->3,704ms (5.1x, drop-in, recommended), naive memo 19,048->2,174ms (8.8x, needs explicit invalidation at 4 replaceState/pushState sites).
